Derive the equations of a model

Source: R/derive.R
sbml_odes.Rd

sbml_odes() turns a model into what an ODE solver needs: the states, the right-hand side of each, the assignments evaluated before the right-hand sides at every time, and the constants. sbml_initial_state() gives the states' values at time 0.

Usage

sbml_odes(m)

sbml_initial_state(m)

Arguments

m

An sbml_model.

Value

sbml_odes() returns a list:

  • states: a data frame with the state's name, the model symbol it belongs to, and its kind ("species", "compartment", ...);

  • rhs: a named list of expressions, the time derivative of each state;

  • assignments: a named list of expressions in evaluation order;

  • constants: a named numeric vector of the constants' values;

  • initial: the states' values at time 0, as sbml_initial_state();

  • species: for each species, whether its symbol is an amount and its compartment, to convert between amounts and concentrations;

  • events: one list per event with its id, trigger, initial_value, persistent, priority and delay expressions (NULL when absent), use_values_from_trigger_time, and assignments, a named list of expressions by target.

sbml_initial_state() returns a named numeric vector.

Details

Species whose symbol is a concentration are integrated as concentrations, except in a compartment whose size can change, where the amount is integrated (as the state .amount.<id>) and the concentration is an assignment. Reaction ids are assignments holding the reaction's rate. Function definitions are inlined, local parameters become constants named .local.<reaction>.<id>, and rateOf() is replaced by the right-hand side it refers to.

Errors

  • zusbml_unsupported for algebraic rules (the model is then a DAE), the delay csymbol and fast reactions, each naming the element.

  • zusbml_derive_error for an assignment cycle, a missing value, or a name the model does not define, naming the ids involved in its ids field.

Examples

m <- sbml_read(system.file("extdata", "decay.xml", package = "zusbml"))
eq <- sbml_odes(m)
eq$rhs
#> $S1
#> -R1/C
#> 
#> $S2
#> R1/C
#> 
sbml_initial_state(m)
#> S1 S2 
#>  1  0
